fact: The Secretary of State for Finance presents the Portal do Munícipe as a Ministry of Finance tool, run with the finance ministry's SETIC-FP IT service, that the municipalities use.

The Portal is a web service at municipal.minfin.gov.ao, reached through the internet, with 547 services, so the record is held in the Ministry of Finance's system and not in each municipality; the article dates the briefing to November 2021 (published 2021-11-17).
The Portal do Munícipe holds the records and management of residents and their households and tracks the whole cycle of fees, licences and fines billed by local administrations; payment is by RUPE.
The Ministry of Finance describes the Portal as a centralised technological solution, web-accessed, with revenue deposited in a Treasury sub-account (SUB-CUT).
The Secretary of State for Finance said the Portal was implemented in all 164 municipalities (164 of 164, Ministry of Finance), with some telecommunications challenges for some administrations.
The Ministry of Finance launched and runs the Portal under Presidential Decree 47/18.
The Ministry of Finance officially launched the Portal do Munícipe on 10 November 2021 across the 164 municipalities.

The Ministry of Finance said it had created the technical conditions for the Portal do Munícipe in 152 of 164 municipalities, 12 not yet covered (Finance technical group member, briefing of 15 August 2019).
Decree 47/18 requires municipal fees to be collected through the Portal and paid by RUPE, so the centre sees the amounts moved; no register of payers is described.
The Portal is a centralised tool that lets central bodies see the amounts local administrations collect.
The Ministry of Finance accelerated the Portal's rollout from October 2018 under Decree 47/18, with AGT placing an official in each administration.
